# Chat Input Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well as snippets of Piton.

### Shape

#### Description

Input on the left, send button on the right.
<Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to the HarnessIntegrationScope
Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

#### Tabs

```
overview: The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec, with a chain button between them that selects both, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip.
Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to the chain to Spec and back to Code, <Shift+Tab> the other way, and focus remains in the chat input.
chain: A small square button, half the height of the tabs and vertically centred on them, with no focus border.
Inactive, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and Code and Spec sit apart with a gap between them wide enough that the chain sits in the gap without overlapping either tab.
Active, it shows a joined chain at full opacity, both tabs are selected, and Code and Spec animate closer together until they meet beneath the chain, which overlaps both and covers the seam so they read as one locked tab. Deactivating it animates them apart again.
The chain never moves: it stays at the same place in both states, and only the tabs slide toward or away from it.
```

#### System Prompt

The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt. The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as set in the project's piton.config.pi.

##### Code

We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit the spec located in <spec location>.

##### Spec

We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit the code located in <code location>.

##### Both

We're working on both the code located in <code location> and the spec located in <spec location>. Edit both of them.

A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

#### Escape

Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat input.

#### Grow To Fit

The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button, and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

#### Auto Focus

The chat input should be auto-focused.

#### Syntax Highlighting

Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

#### Lsp

[LSP](../../lsp/LSP.md)

#### Harness Mentions

```
overview: Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@` offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself. The placeholder mentions both.
trigger: A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one they never reach the [LSP](../../lsp/LSP.md).
offered: Skills and commands are those of the selected ProjectDirectoryScope, of the user, and of the user's enabled plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before matches anywhere in it, then by name.
accepting: Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs that skill or command. Mentions work without the [LSP](../../lsp/LSP.md).
```

#### Hidden Anchor

While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes, they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/HarnessIntegrationScope.md)

use /lib
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        overview:
            The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
            gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec,
            with a chain button between them that selects both, reading
            "Code and Spec" as its tooltip.

            Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to the
            chain to Spec and back to Code, <Shift+Tab> the other way, and
            focus remains in the chat input.

        chain:
            A small square button, half the height of the tabs and vertically
            centred on them, with no focus border.

            Inactive, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and
            Code and Spec sit apart with a gap between them wide enough that
            the chain sits in the gap without overlapping either tab.

            Active, it shows a joined chain at full opacity, both tabs are
            selected, and Code and Spec animate closer together until they
            meet beneath the chain, which overlaps both and covers the seam
            so they read as one locked tab. Deactivating it animates them
            apart again.

            The chain never moves: it stays at the same place in both states,
            and only the tabs slide toward or away from it.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        both:
            We're working on both the code located in <code location> and the
            spec located in <spec location>. Edit both of them.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per
        visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft
        wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window
        is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button,
        and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign
            followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are
            requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter,
            digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only
            inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one
            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

content.text:
I built the Ask behaviour: a question now runs on its own, apart from any Code or Spec task. It slides up out of the chat input as a single row while it's thinking, then expands into its full task table once it's done. Both new tests pass, and so does everything else except one palette test that doesn't touch this work.

**How it behaves**
- **Runs separately:** sending from the Ask tab runs straight away, even while a task is running. It never queues, doesn't add to the task list, and doesn't block the queue. The send button reads "Send" on the Ask tab even while the harness is busy.
- **While thinking:** a panel sits directly above the tabs showing one row of the task table: the type badge, the latest thing the harness did, and a status. It slides up out of the input when it appears.
- **When done:** the same panel expands, still above the tabs, into a heading (status and the question) and the full task table, which scrolls past 320px.
- **Closing:** an X button closes the panel. If the question is still running, closing stops it.

**Where it lives**
- **`src/prompt_mode.rs`:** the ask runs as its own task with its own panel. I moved the table's status cell into a shared function, and the three places that set up a prompt's hidden anchor now share one function.
- **`src/hidden_anchor.rs`:** questions are saved under `.suspense/asks`, not `.suspense/history`, so they don't come back as tasks when the project is reopened.
- **`src/chat_input.rs`:** the send button no longer says "Queue" on the Ask tab.

**Choices you may want to change**
- Asking a new question replaces and stops one that's still running; you only get one at a time.
- A question's output isn't saved, so it's gone once the panel is closed or the app restarts.
- A running question counts as work, so quitting asks you to confirm.

**Tests:** two new tests. One checks that a question runs while a task is working without being queued, touching that task or writing to the history. The other checks that it's one row directly above the tabs while running and the full table once finished.

**The palette failure:** `palette::tests::lists_files_by_path_leaving_out_ignored_ones` expects `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` in the file list but doesn't get it. `palette.rs` is untouched, and my changes don't affect how files are listed. My guess is that something in your environment ignores `.claude` (a global gitignore, say), but I haven't checked.

I didn't edit the spec. `ChatInputScope` doesn't mention the Ask tab or this behaviour yet, so it will need updating on the spec side.
